summary: Snapshot 2026-09-26. Google Trends and Wikipedia had no health topics today (sports, entertainment, politics), so the calls below come from journals, press releases and news pickup, checked by web search. Six topics from the last snapshot kept building across more sources: HRT and blood clots, REM sleep, the menopause blood-protein 'fingerprint', Galleri, peptides and GLP-1 nutrition. Best early bets: (1) The BMJ HRT clot study, which is in trade and medical press but has little mainstream or creator coverage; (2) a SELECT reanalysis in the European Heart Journal finding that weight loss alone doesn't explain semaglutide's heart benefit (ESC press release, barely picked up so far); (3) the Galleri story now has a twist: an FDA advisory panel backed the test on Sep 23 (6–4 on whether it works) even though it missed its main goal in the NHS trial; (4) the Surrey 'sugar rationing' study linking sugar in the first 1,000 days of life to adult anxiety (a natural experiment in 45,000 people, just reaching US News and Euronews). Seasonal hooks are flu shot timing and mosquito-borne infections (West Nile at a 10-year high in San Diego, local dengue in Florida). A correction to the brief: the light-at-night heart study came out Sep 9 and has already been covered by CNN and NBC, so it's a second-wave evergreen topic, not an early one. The GLP-1 muscle-loss 'new therapy' is a mouse study, so it has to be framed that way. Everything involving prescription drugs (HRT, semaglutide, weekly insulin, peptides) is marked caution: talk about how to read the evidence, never doses or telling people to switch or stop.

candidates.topic: Oral vs patch/gel menopause HRT and blood clots: 1M-woman Danish nationwide study (The BMJ, Sep 23)
candidates.angle: 'Is HRT dangerous?' is the wrong question. How you take it matters. In this study, oral estrogen was linked to higher clot risk at any dose or duration, while transdermal showed no overall increase. Explain absolute vs relative risk and give a 'questions to ask your clinician' checklist. No dosing.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot in a row. It has spread from BMJ press to Healio, News-Medical, Medical Xpress and cardiology trade press, but consumer outlets and creators have barely covered it. Menopause content is booming with our core 35–55 women viewers.

evidence.signal: Nationwide nested case-control study of 1,060,082 women aged 50–69
Oral linked to higher clot risk regardless of dose or duration; transdermal no overall increase
Clinical press pickup Sep 24

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of Ozempic/Wegovy's heart benefit: SELECT mediation analysis (European Heart Journal, Sep 23)
candidates.angle: If it's not the pounds, what is it? Waist size, inflammation (hsCRP) and blood sugar each explain part of it, but some of the benefit is still unexplained. Frame it as 'why your waist beats your scale' plus what this means for everyone, whether or not they take GLP-1s.
keywords: semaglutide heart benefit not weight loss
candidates.why_now: Fresh ESC press release and EHJ paper, picked up by Medical Xpress, with no mainstream or creator coverage yet. GLP-1 is the biggest health search category, and the 'waist, not weight' takeaway works for everyone.

evidence.signal: Mediation analysis of the SELECT trial published Sep 23
'Weight loss alone does not explain lower heart disease' (waist 64%, hsCRP 42%, body weight 19.5% mediation, wide CIs)
Early news pickup

candidates.topic: Galleri multi-cancer blood test: missed its main goal in the 142,942-person NHS RCT, yet an FDA panel backed it (6–4 on effectiveness)
candidates.angle: 'Should you buy the $949 cancer blood test?' Explain what 'missed its main goal' means (no significant drop in stage III–IV cancers), what it did show (fewer stage IV cases, more cancers found by screening), false positives and cost, and why the panel still voted yes. A calm consumer guide, not a verdict.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–14 days (spikes again on the FDA decision)
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. The NEJM/Nature Medicine results came out alongside a 6–4 FDA panel vote, and BMJ news ran 'fails… but FDA still endorses it'. Covered by STAT and trade press, but few consumer explainers. An FDA approval decision is still to come, which will set off another search spike.

evidence.signal: Effect of MCED screening on late-stage diagnosis
'Galleri cancer test fails to meet main aim in NHS trial, but FDA still endorses it' (Sep 25)
FDA expert panel endorses Galleri, Sep 23
'FDA panel narrowly backs multi-cancer blood test despite doubts it works'

candidates.topic: Postwar sugar rationing and adult anxiety: less sugar in the first 1,000 days linked to 33% lower anxiety risk (Translational Psychiatry, 45,000 UK Biobank adults)
candidates.angle: A natural experiment from 1950s Britain. The end of sugar rationing gives a rare, cleaner look at whether early sugar shapes the adult brain. Cover what it can and can't prove, why women were affected more, and practical toddler sugar guidance (AAP/NHS: no added sugar under 2) without shaming parents.
candidates.why_now: Surrey press release, then US News, Euronews and Yahoo within days. The story is irresistible and still has almost no creator coverage. It works for both parents and anyone curious about the history.

evidence.signal: Press release: sugar exposure in first 1,000 days linked to adult anxiety
Mainstream pickup Sep 24
International pickup Sep 25

candidates.topic: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases (PLOS Medicine, 95,559 UK Biobank wearers)
candidates.angle: 'Your tracker's REM number, decoded.' What ~48 extra minutes of REM was linked to (46% lower dementia risk, 26% lower heart failure risk), why the link is observational and could run in reverse, how accurate wearables are at sleep staging, and evidence-based ways to protect REM (alcohol, regular timing, enough total sleep).
keywords: how to get more REM sleep
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. It has spread to Inc, ScienceAlert, MNT, HealthDay TV and Yahoo, and a KSNV segment on sleep consistency. Mainstream is catching on and short-form creators are next.

evidence.signal: Release Sep 23
Consumer pickup with study details
Science press pickup

candidates.topic: Menopause leaves a 16-protein blood 'fingerprint' linked to brain aging and dementia risk (Nature Medicine)
candidates.angle: Why women's dementia risk isn't just 'living longer'. Explain what the protein signature is, that it's a research tool and not a test you can buy, and the steps with solid evidence (blood pressure, hearing, exercise, sleep). Pairs naturally with the HRT clot video.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. Medical Xpress ran it Sep 25, three days after publication, which shows slow but steady spread. Plus a Fox piece on a '10-year rule' for brain fog, so brain fog searches are active.

evidence.signal: 'Menopause leaves a fingerprint that may predict dementia risk' Sep 25

candidates.topic: GLP-1 muscle loss: new RNA therapy halved lean-mass loss, but only in mice (PNAS, Northwestern)
candidates.angle: Use the headline as a hook for the 'what actually works now' answer. The mouse result: 5.5% vs 10% lean mass lost. What works in humans today: resistance training and enough protein, backed by trials. Call out the 'new therapy' hype clearly.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Wegovy
candidates.why_now: NewsNation and Crain's say 'new therapy could stop GLP-1 muscle loss', which is likely to be over-hyped on TikTok. 'Ozempic muscle loss' is a constant high-volume search, and the Sep 23 GLP-1 nutrient-deficiency story is still circulating.

evidence.signal: RNA therapy + semaglutide preserved lean mass in mice (PNAS, Sep 25)
Science press pickup
GLP-1 drugs linked to nutrient deficiencies in ~1 in 6 young patients (related hook)

candidates.topic: Fecal microbiota transplant fails for IBS in phase 3 REFIT2 trial (The Lancet, Sep 24)
candidates.angle: 'Poop transplants for IBS don't work, and that's useful to know.' Explain why earlier small trials looked promising, what the placebo-controlled trial found, and which IBS approaches do have evidence (low-FODMAP diet under guidance, gut-directed CBT/hypnotherapy, soluble fibre). Also a warning about DIY FMT.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. It's a big negative result in a gut-health area full of hype, with no creator coverage yet. The gut-health audience is huge, and a myth-busting angle suits our brand.

evidence.signal: REFIT2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial

candidates.topic: Flu season 2026–27: new mRNA flu shot for 50+, subclade K, and 'when should I get it?'
candidates.angle: A practical fall explainer: why doctors are urging young, healthy people too, whether to get it in October or wait, what's new this year, and how to handle the confusing federal vaccine-policy news. We stay pro-vaccine and link to guidance.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. Local TV is pushing flu-shot messages, CDC recommendations are stalled (Medical Xpress), and Roche Xofluza generic deals are in the news. Searches climb every year from late September into October.

evidence.signal: 'Doctors urge everyone, including young and healthy, to get flu shot this fall'
CDC vaccine policy recommendations stalled

candidates.topic: Vitamin K2 + D3 slowed the rise in coronary calcium scores by 21% (DANCODE RCT, Circulation / ESC 2026)
candidates.angle: 'The supplement combo that actually has an RCT.' What a calcium score is, what 21% slower progression does and doesn't mean (no proof yet of fewer heart attacks), who was studied, and a warning about warfarin interactions (see your clinician).
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. Nutraceutical trade press is now covering it, and supplement brands will start pushing it soon. Get in first with a balanced take before the marketing wave.

evidence.signal: Trade pickup Sep 25

candidates.topic: Peptides (BPC-157 & co.): big promises, thin human evidence, shifting FDA compounding rules
candidates.angle: 'What's actually been tested in humans?' A scorecard for each popular peptide: human RCTs vs rodent-only data, contamination risk from grey-market vials, and where the rules stand. Never present unapproved peptides as effective.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. Outside Magazine published 'Peptides: Huge Promises, Unproven Hype' on Sep 26, and influencer peptide content is everywhere. Demand for a skeptical explainer is high.

evidence.signal: 'Peptides: Huge Promises, Unproven Hype' Sep 26

candidates.topic: Sleeping with light on linked to thicker, stiffer hearts (European Heart Journal, 11,071 UK Biobank wrist light sensors)
candidates.angle: 'The 3-lux rule.' How dark your bedroom needs to be, a cheap setup (blackout, eye mask, phone face-down), and why these are early heart changes, not disease. Can be paired with the REM story as a 'sleep that protects your body' series.
candidates.why_now: Published Sep 9 and covered by CNN, NBC and TIME. Second-wave lifestyle coverage (EatingWell, Sep 26) shows continued interest. Longer daylight-saving nights in the fall make it a good time for bedroom-light content.

evidence.signal: >3 lux linked to thicker left ventricle walls and reduced strain
Mainstream coverage Sep 9

candidates.topic: Strokes nearly doubled in adults 20–54 since the 1990s (Neurology)
candidates.angle: 'Stroke isn't an old-person disease anymore.' Cover the likely drivers (blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, drugs, migraine with aura), BE-FAST warning signs, and one number to know: your blood pressure.
keywords: why are young people having strokes
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. It has moved from the journal to the NY Post. A JAMA Netw Open paper on young-adult stroke adds support. Its fear-and-solution shape works well in Shorts.

evidence.signal: 'Strokes nearly double among adults under a certain age'
Antithrombotic therapy and bleeding after ischemic stroke in young adults

candidates.topic: FDA approves Onswik (efsitora), the first once-weekly insulin for type 2 diabetes (Sep 24)
candidates.angle: '52 shots a year instead of 365.' What weekly basal insulin is, who it's for, what the QWINT trials showed, and the questions to bring to your diabetes team. No dosing and no switching advice.
candidates.why_now: Just approved and covered by STAT, Medscape and Fox 4. Consumer explainers are thin, and many people in our age range have a parent or partner with type 2 diabetes.

evidence.signal: FDA approval press release
'Lilly wins approval for once-weekly insulin shot'

candidates.topic: Mosquito season isn't over: West Nile at a 10-year high in San Diego, local dengue emergency in Florida
candidates.angle: 'Why late-September mosquito bites matter': which symptoms need a doctor, who's at highest risk from West Nile (50+), the repellents with evidence (DEET, picaridin, oil of lemon eucalyptus), and standing-water checks.
candidates.why_now: West Nile death reported in Orange County, San Diego cases at a 10-year high, Tampa Bay counties under a dengue emergency, and a Powassan virus research release. Local news is heating up, but there's no single national explainer.

evidence.signal: West Nile cases in San Diego County hit 10-year high
Florida county declares dengue emergency

candidates.topic: 10 diets compared for biological aging: no single winner, consistency wins (Nature Communications, ~7,500 adults)
candidates.angle: 'Stop diet-hopping.' What the study compared, why sticking to any reasonably healthy pattern beat chasing the 'best' one, and a guide to the traits all good diets share. Avoid extreme-diet framing.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. It has reached Yahoo Health, and a Medical Xpress MIND diet piece and a Newsweek 'one simple food change' story show the diet-longevity theme is active.

candidates.angle: 'The health habit nobody tracks.' Loneliness vs isolation, how big the effect is compared with familiar risks, and small evidence-based ways to reconnect (weekly routines, volunteering, group exercise).
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot. It spread to US News and Inc ('This everyday habit can cost you 5 healthy years'). Its warm, positive framing fits our brand, and competition is moderate.

evidence.signal: 'Loneliness, Isolation Can Strip Away Years Of Healthy Life'

candidates.angle: A guide for parents in our 25–55 audience: what the study found, why it's an association and not proof of cause, and evidence-backed digital habits for families. Give no weight or eating details, and include helpline resources.

candidates.why_now: CNN covered it Sep 25, and 'what age for a smartphone' is a recurring search spike around back-to-school. Few science-led explainers exist.

evidence.signal: Smartphone ownership and eating disorder symptoms in early adolescence
'Giving a tween a smartphone may increase the risk of body image issues'

candidates.topic: 'Detox microplastics from your body' tips: what the evidence does and doesn't support
candidates.angle: Fact-check the Verywell-style '5 ways to get rid of microplastics' lists. Reducing exposure (heat, plastic containers, bottled water) has some logic. 'Flushing them out' with supplements or saunas has essentially no evidence.
